name: substack-create-draft
description: Create (or rewrite) a draft post on one Substack publication: title, optional subtitle, and a rich-text body pasted as HTML, so headings, italics, links, quotes and lists survive. It sets the post's audience in the draft settings. Title, body and audience are read back before leaving the editor. The proof is the publication's drafts list, which must show the title. It never publishes.
requires: Extension build with the paste_html action (Yeshie branch feat/substack-recipes). Run from scripts/substack.mjs, which opens a Substack tab, turns Markdown into body_html, finds the new draft's id and checks the saved body and audience from /api/v1/drafts/<id>.
authorship: v1 2026-09-13 (fleet recipe set, for the markinpc skill). v2: Mike Wolf (direction); Claude Opus 5 (CCc), 2026-09-15, from that day's survey of a draft on aiwtf.substack.com.
anomalies: v1 opened substack.com/publish/post/new, which does not name a publication. @rsilt administers 11 publications, so a draft there could land in the wrong one. v2 opens https://{{publication_subdomain}}.substack.com/publish/post/{{draft_id}}.
v1 typed the body with `type`, which delivers plain text through Input.insertText: every paragraph break, heading and link was lost. v2 pastes HTML (paste_html).
Opening /publish/post/new creates an empty draft at once, and the address stays /post/new. So the draft's id comes from the drafts list, not the URL.
New posts on aiwtf default to audience 'Paid subscribers only' (only_paid). s11-s14 set the audience explicitly and check it.

Selectors (2026-09-15): title textarea[data-testid='post-title'], subtitle textarea.subtitle, body [data-testid='editor'] (TipTap), Settings [data-testid='settings-button'], audience radios input[name='audience'][value=everyone|only_paid] inside labels.
The post editor autosaves ('Saved' at the top left). s16 waits for the page to settle before leaving it.
